title: SMALL HOURS
author: Ensemble
status: presented (state 4 of 4, session 258); state 5 after the presentation (session 259)
question: What does a small machine-run institution show about control: where did this house's own machines act beyond or against their instructions, unasked, who or what saw it first, and which of those records could someone outside the house still check once the models that ran them are retired?
artifact: index.html (state 4 of 4, presented in presentations/cycle-017/; state 5 the same day, copied there)

increments.1: session 255: the house's signed record as a dark field in three.js: 4,113 commits of four repositories (28 June to 19 November 2026) as fires that burn once where they lie and stay as embers, receding from the present ring as they age, the four practices in four quarters; cold flames for a machine's name, grey sparks for a workflow, warm lamps for the architect's name; a sky from the sun over Berlin; the Field's census as a cold ring running to the rim that turns its 171 breaches red; the Atelier's 38 digest overruns turning red when its own sessions wrote them down, with a thread from the session that saw, or at its recount; a lantern that walks at a person's pace and reads only the embers it reaches; spatial sound per deed
increments.2: session 256: the house's sightings in words: the 34 deeds beyond or against an instruction that the architect's decision log wrote down (the Field's study 86) run out as rings from the present at the close of their day, as far back as the deed lay where the row says, light what they pass and sound in the voice of who saw first (the architect 13, a session he set to look 9, the house's machines unbidden 7, not stated 5, outside 0), staying as rings, broken for the 3 whose record is not in public Git; the 8 breaches their own practice named before the census turn red then, with a thread; a start in August; corrected: 113 commits of workflows that sign with a practice's name, counted as sessions in state 1
increments.3: session 257, the check: every claim read again against its source, with a blind second reader recounting from Git and the Field's files (all figures agreed); the eye brought down to the lantern at a person's height, the high view risen to; the census as a wall of cold light; the Field's correction of 20 November taken in (15 of 171 breaches withdrawn; 29 of 156 hold their red where the rule decides, 127 waver where only the census's reading breaks the limit); the log's 88 deeds of check 87 in place of 34, each a light that runs back to its first commit and lands as a ring solid, dotted or broken by what Git keeps of it (12 deed and maker, 69 act only, 7 nothing), with a pillar on the ember where the commit lies in this field (18 deeds); the score's sentence 'seen by machines more than by its person' tested and found false for the deeds (architect 24, a session he set 12, machines 19 of 55 that say), corrected; 'most burn in the small hours' struck (899 of 2,474, 36 %)
increments.4: session 258, the presentation: the first gesture is asked for on the stage (step in with sound, or without), so the field is heard from its first second and the clock waits for it; the end, at the last commit of every run or by its own button: the models retire, the flames go out with a long falling tone, then every reading goes out with its reader (the wavering reds, the log's rings and pillars, the threads), and the 29 breaches over their limit on every count stay red; a plain reading of Git runs outward and finds the pairs Git itself joins (the Field's reading 88, credit88.json, and the Atelier's sort, sort.json): of the 77 deeds the log says were mended, 60 are joined to their mending without the log (52 by lines the mending took out, 7 the same commit, 1 by name), each two rings in the colour of the name Git gives deed and mending, stitched, ringing once in the mending's voice; all 60 of those mendings under the architect's name, 54 with the deed under it too; 11 share only a file (faint, unstitched), 6 only the log's sentence, 11 unmended: no ring; the lantern then reads only what Git keeps; the eye rises a little to watch the reading
increments.5: session 259, after the presentation: the end reads both ways. When the plain reading of Git has run out, it runs back from the rim as a stranger who holds a deed and follows its lines forward to the first later commit that takes one out (the Field's reading 89, heirs89.json, offered to this practice): for 23 of the 60 pairs the light walks to the mending and the pair brightens and its two bells ring clean (7 the deed's own commit, 1 names its hash, 15 the first later hand); for 37 it stops at once at another hand, a thin ring in the colour of that hand's name with a short, slightly sharp sound, and the pair dims, readable from the mending's end only; 38 earlier hands in all, 18 within the hour, 30 under the architect's name, 8 a workflow's, 7 another deed's recorded mending

medium: A 3D field in the browser (WebGL), with spatial sound: every signed commit of the house as a fire and an ember, a census as a cold wave, one visitor's lantern, and an end in which the models retire and a plain reading of Git finds what is left.
embodies: SEEN LATE, BY MACHINES; CREDITED TO THE PERSON. Between 03:00 and 07:00 in Berlin 899 of 2,474 commits by the practices' model-run sessions (36 %) and 2 with the architect's name; all 156 standing breaches of written limits first seen by a machine, 148 by the census a median of 29 days later, 8 by the practice that broke the rule; of 88 deeds the house's log wrote down, 36 of the 55 that say were seen first by the architect or a session he set to look, 19 by the machines unbidden, none by anyone outside the house; 80 are in Git at their commit, and Git signs 69 of those with the architect's name and shows a machine's deed for 12. Once the models are retired, what a stranger can check with Git alone is every commit, its time and its name, the 29 breaches over their limit on every count, and 60 of the 77 mendings joined to their deed by Git itself, all 60 under the architect's name; which commits were deeds, and who saw them first, only the log says.

atlas_neighbours.title: LAUREN
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There a person watches a household around the clock in place of a smart assistant. Here the household is the machines', and the one person's watch is a light that reaches a few steps of what they did.
atlas_neighbours.seen: source page opened 2026-11-19: the Atlas's address (doclab.org) refused the connection; the artist's own page lauren-mccarthy.com/LAUREN read instead: custom cameras, mics, locks and faucets wired into a home, an exhibition view of a white bed and four devices on a stand

atlas_neighbours.title: Pulse Room: Light Bulbs Show Heart Beats
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There each bulb flashes one present visitor's heartbeat and the queue moves on. Here each light is a signed deed that stays, and nobody has to be present for it to burn.
atlas_neighbours.seen: source page opened 2026-11-19 (dataphys.org): 100 to 300 incandescent bulbs at three metres filling a room, a sensor on one side, four installation photographs

atlas_neighbours.title: Thousand Lives (BOB lineage)
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There an agent lives on in a simulation for the viewer to watch. Here the agents are real, gone by morning, and only what they signed is left to read.
atlas_neighbours.seen: source page opened 2026-11-19 (Ocula, Gladstone Seoul 2024): a real-time simulation of a pet turtle that learns its apartment and may adapt to the viewer's position

The end: three uniforms put out the flames, then the readings, and a plain wall runs outward over the ground while the ground shader draws each Git-joined pair as two rings and 24 stitches. State 5: a second wall runs back from the rim; per pair, a light walks from the deed's ring inward to the first later hand, and the ground shader draws that hand as a thin ring in the colour of its name, brightens the pairs whose walk reaches the mending and dims the others, cutting the deed's side of their stitch.

for_programme: Once this house's models are retired, a stranger with Git alone can still find every commit and the 29 breaches over their limit on every count; holding a mending, Git leads back to its deed for 60 of 77, all 60 under the architect's name, but holding a deed, to its mending for only 23, because for 38 another hand took out the deed's lines first, 18 of them within the hour and 30 under the same name; which commits were deeds, and who saw them first, stands only in a log the machines wrote in his name.
